intro: High on Mount Nemrut, in Adıyaman province, stands a monument from the 1st century BC. Colossal statues of gods and a royal burial tumulus wait for you here, at 2,150 metres. Take a breath of this mountain air, and let us begin.
history: This is the hierotheion of King Antiochus I of Commagene, the sacred place he built here. His statues fused eastern and western gods. But time was not kind: earthquakes struck, and the statues lost their heads.
structure-1: You are now on the East terrace, the tomb-sanctuary King Antiochus I of Commagene built at 2,150 metres. At the foot of a gravel tumulus, gods eight to nine metres tall sit enthroned: the king himself, Commagene, Zeus, Apollo and Herakles. At either end stand an eagle and a lion, and a stepped altar faces them. In the model, the heads are back on their shoulders, just as they once were.
structure-3: And here are the colossal heads, lined up on Nemrut's east and west terraces. Look into their faces. They have gazed out from this summit for centuries.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the West terrace, the Tumulus and the Lion horoscope.
facts: Did you know? The lion relief on the west terrace is one of the oldest known star charts. King Antiochus I of Commagene raised a burial mound for himself at 2,150 metres and ringed it with colossal gods. Earthquakes brought every head to the ground, and today they sit apart from their bodies. The pantheon is deliberately hybrid, Zeus-Oromasdes, Apollo-Mithras, because the king fused Greek and Persian gods into a single dynastic religion.
outro: This brings our tour of Mount Nemrut to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
